lead.text: The Great Black-backed Gull is a large, broad-winged and heavily built gull with a thick neck and a very heavy bill.
In Sweden it breeds along the coasts and prefers the outer islets and skerries.

fieldMarks.text: Adults have blackish upperparts and white underparts, breast, head, tail and rump
Yellow bill with a clear red spot at the gonys, red orbital ring and yellow iris
Large white spots on the flight feathers show when the bird is perched
Sexes look alike, but females are often only as large as Herring Gulls

voice.text: The main call is a deep, often hoarse and sometimes loud "kau" or "krau".
It resembles the calls of Lesser Black-backed and Herring Gulls but is much darker, typically hoarse and gravelly.
The laughing display call is shorter and slower than in Lesser Black-backed and Herring Gulls.

whereWhen.text: A partial migrant, it breeds on Swedish coasts, preferably on outer islets and skerries.
Inland it is found less often, but it breeds by the larger lakes.
In winter it occurs at sea and along the coasts, as long as there is open water.
It is reported all year and from all 21 counties.
The Swedish Red List 2025 lists it as Endangered (EN).

behaviour.text: It feeds mainly on fish caught alive, but adapts its diet to conditions.
It can kill weakened seabirds such as auks, smaller gulls and shearwaters.
It is shy and watchful, and more of a loner than many other gulls.
In flight it looks calm, with slow wingbeats.

text.text: The Great Black-backed Gull has greyish pink legs at all ages, while the adult Lesser Black-backed Gull has yellow legs.
Young Great Black-backed Gulls are clearly chequered black and white, not dull greyish like young Herring Gulls.
